The nearly-Gamma class is the class that Chatterjee's scaling relation later assumes.

named_target_nodes.title: Attempt on Fourier entropy versus total influence
named_target_nodes.body_excerpt:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Fourier entropy versus total influence exact calculation or structural obstruction Result: Discarding the Boolean constraint destroys the claim: the probability measure uniform on the n singleton subsets has entropy log2(n) but mean subset size1. It cannot be the squared spectrum of a Boolean function when n>=2. Check: If all Fourier mass were on singletons, f=sum_i a_i*x_i with a_i=plus/minus1/sqrt(n). In f^2 the coefficient of x_i*x_j is2*a_i*a_j, nonzero for distinct i,j, whereas Boolean f requires f^2=1. This independently exhibits the violated Fourier convolution identity. Obstruction: Entropy versus mean cardinality alone is insufficient. Any proof must use the nonlinear identities imposed by f^2=1; no dimension-free inequality exploiting all of them is obtained.

named_target_nodes.title: Fourier entropy-influence: reduction to small-influence functions, a 7.05 floor for restriction inductions, and read-once formulas over AND, OR, XOR, NOT
named_target_nodes.body_excerpt: The Fourier entropy-influence conjecture is equivalent to its restriction to Boolean functions all of whose influences are below any fixed tau: a coordinate of influence at least tau has restriction drop Delta_i <= (2/ln 2 + log2(e/tau)) Inf_i, so a violation localizes to a subcube on which every influence is small and the restriction step fails at every coordinate. On self-compositions of Numaro's record function the restriction-step constant rho_0 = min_i Delta_i/Inf_i is 6.3290, 6.8901 and 7.0519 at 324, 5832 and 104976 variables (limit about 7.1116), so no potential-free coordinate induction can give a constant below 7.05. The XOR gate inequality is certified, so read-once formulas over AND, OR, XOR and NOT satisfy H <= 6.4573 I; a prime monotone 7-input gate breaks the read-once potential behind that bound; the five prime 3-input classes (one-hot, MAJ3, EQ3, MUX, Q3) are proved, while fan-in 3 at 6.4573 in general is numerical only. Per-coordinate erasure bounds fail even for monotone functions (majority with one flipped point gives ratio at least (n - 3 log2 n)/2). The full conjecture remains open.
